newsitem.title: UK: LME copper falls sharply, widespread liquidation.
newsitem.headline: LME copper falls sharply, widespread liquidation.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper prices fell sharply in widespread liquidation on Wednesday, traders said.
Prices breached $2,400 a tonne in the morning kerb session and traded at $2,368, compared with the previous close of $2,437. Copper had touched six-week lows on the LME in nervous trading on Tuesday.
Traders said the fall below expected support at $2,400 now looked to take the market to $2,350 a tonne or possibly lower.
Widespread liquidation and sell-stops were behind the move, which at one stage took prices to a six-week low of $2,355, but there appeared no fresh fundamental news behind the fall.
However, in nervous trading some short-covering emerged to offset the fall. Final three months business was at $2,373, well down on Tuesday's LME kerb close of $2,437.
